Why these are skips, not ports: each test exercises POSIX shell semantics (CI step bodies under bash, host scripts, sh command stubs) that have no Windows equivalent; Linux CI keeps running all of them.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Discovered from majestic-depilatory-beetle. The advisory `sweep (windows)` job deselects the 143 tests in `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/posix-shell.args` (23 modules, runs at `b4e0d01b649`, 2026-11-15/16).

Root cause, confirmed from Windows job 133527199439 (run 43932173744): these tests execute POSIX shell, by one of three routes, none of which exists on Windows:

1. `bash ...` / `bash -c` (e.g. `tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py` runs workflow step bodies). On the runner `bash` is the WSL launcher with no distribution: it prints UTF-16 `Windows Subsystem for Linux has no installed distributions` and exits 1 (seen as `W\x00i\x00n\x00d\x00o\x00w\x00s` in the asserts).
2. A shebang stub (`#!/bin/sh` or `#!/usr/bin/env python3`) written to a temp dir and run directly or found via `PATH`; Windows cannot execute it (`OSError: [WinError 193] %1 is not a valid Win32 application`, or `[WinError 2]` when looked up on `PATH`).
3. The literal `/bin/sh`, drive-relative on Windows.

The same root cause accounts for 21 tests filed under `path-separators.args` (bug arctic-unsecular-esok): `tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py` (1), `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py` (3), `tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py` (1), `tests/integration/test_reclaim_comment_echo_history.py` (2), `tests/scripts/test_cast_gerrit_verified_vote.py` (6 of its 8; the two `*_fails_before_ssh` tests never run the stub and stay unmarked), `tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py` (1), `tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py` (1), `tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers.py` (5 `four_environment_matrix` cases, which symlink `bash` into a PATH-only bin dir), `tests/unit/workflow/test_snapshot_stream_bounds_093a.py` (1, a python-shebang stub). Each stubs a command with a shell or shebang script.

Exception: the 7 `tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py` lines are a separator defect in `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:99,160` (`str(p.relative_to(...))`), not a shell one; bug arctic-unsecular-esok fixes and un-deselects them.

## Approach

What these tests exercise is POSIX shell behaviour (CI step bodies, host scripts, command stubs), which has no Windows equivalent to port to, so each gets a capability skip, keyed on the capability rather than `os.name`, following the precedent of `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py` (commit `ed501817343`, `os.access("/bin/sh", os.X_OK)`).

- Add to the existing shared helper module `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py` (no new `tests/_*.py` mechanism): `posix_shell_available(sh: str = "/bin/sh") -> bool` (`os.access(sh, os.X_OK)`) and `requires_posix_shell = pytest.mark.skipif(not posix_shell_available(), reason="needs a POSIX shell at /bin/sh and shebang-script execution; this host has neither")`. `/bin/sh` is present on every Linux and macOS host, so the skip can never fire on the gating Linux lanes.
- Apply `@requires_posix_shell` to each affected test function. Only where every test in a module runs a shell is it a module mark, appended to any existing marks: `tests/scripts/test_install_sandbox_bwrap.py` becomes `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.scripts, requires_posix_shell]`; `tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_e2e_scenario4.py` and `tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py` (no existing `pytestmark`) get `pytestmark = requires_posix_shell`. `tests/scripts/test_cast_gerrit_verified_vote.py` keeps its `pytestmark = pytest.mark.scripts` and gets per-function marks on the 6 stub-running tests.
- Remove every marked test's line from `posix-shell.args` and the 21 lines from `path-separators.args`. Delete `posix-shell.args` and its `@` line in `.github/workflows/test.yml` once it is empty (after arctic-unsecular-esok removes the 7 manifest lines, whichever lands second deletes it).

Portability: the probe is `os.access` on a fixed path, with no subprocess. On Windows it returns False because `/bin/sh` (drive-relative there) does not exist; it does not depend on `X_OK` semantics, which Windows does not honour.

## Scope

- `tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py`; new `tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_posix_shell.py`
- The 22 non-manifest modules in `posix-shell.args`: `tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py`, `tests/unit/test_session_shims.py`, `tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_e2e_scenario4.py`, `tests/unit/test_child_oracle_fail_open.py`, `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py`, `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`, `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`, `tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py`, `tests/scripts/test_install_sandbox_bwrap.py`, `tests/scripts/test_gerrit_object_store_repair.py`, `tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_inventory.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers.py`, `tests/unit/test_per_session_scratch_guidance.py`, `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py`, `tests/unit/test_harness_shims.py`, `tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py`, `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py`, `tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_entrypoint.py`, `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`, `tests/scripts/test_jira_pressure_test_preflight.py`
- The 9 path-separators modules listed above
- `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/posix-shell.args`, `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/path-separators.args`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`

## Testing

- New `tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_posix_shell.py`: `posix_shell_available` is False for a nonexistent path (unconditional; this is the Windows case), True for an executable temp script, and on any host with `/bin/sh` the shared mark does not skip (so Linux CI never loses these tests). Edge: a file chmod'ed `0o644` is False; that case first checks `os.access(p, os.X_OK)` and calls `pytest.skip("host does not honour POSIX execute bits")` when the host reports it executable anyway (Windows), so it keys on the capability, not `os.name`.
- `make verify` passes with the marked tests still running (not skipped) on Linux.
- Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge; the un-deselected tests report SKIPPED with the reason, and the job succeeds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The class's root cause is recorded on this ticket with the evidence that confirmed it.
- [x] On the merged tree, `pytest -rs` on Linux over the touched modules reports no skip carrying the `requires_posix_shell` reason.
- [x] Every line removed from `posix-shell.args` (and the 21 removed from `path-separators.args`) names a test that passed or skipped with the capability reason in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix (run id recorded in a comment).
- [x] `sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run.
